name: spread_dynamics_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when a 5-second bar's high-low range expands to 2× or more the 5-minute rolling average range, it signals a liquidity stress event — typically a stop-cascade execution, large institutional TWAP block completing, or aggressive momentum algo entry overwhelming resting orders. NIFTY's continuous futures depth means these stress bursts complete within 30-60 seconds and leave a directional overshoot as the aggressive initiator finishes, with resting limit orders on the other side temporarily absorbed. When the per-bar range contracts back below 1.5× normal (stress resolved), NIFTY futures market makers who widened their quotes and delta-hedged during the event begin rebalancing inventory, and VWAP-benchmarked algorithms resume passive fills at their benchmark prices — this systematic reversal flow drives a 40-60% reversion of the spike move within the next 60 seconds. The 5-second resolution lets us enter at the precise moment of stress resolution rather than waiting for a full 1-minute bar confirmation, capturing the first and largest leg of the reversion.

indicators.name: bar_range
indicators.purpose: Per-5s-bar high-low range is the OHLCV proxy for bid-ask spread expansion. In the original, the signal was best_ask - best_bid from order book data. On NIFTY index OHLCV, the bar range captures the same information: when the range suddenly expands, the index is experiencing the same microstructure stress that causes individual stock spreads to widen. Lookback is 1 bar — computed directly each bar.

indicators.name: avg_range_60
indicators.purpose: 5-minute (60 bars) rolling average of bar range establishes the 'normal' volatility baseline for the current session regime. The original used SMA(30) on 1-min bars = 30-minute SMA, which is too stale for 5s resolution where regime can shift in 5-10 minutes. 60 bars (5 min) is long enough to be a stable estimate but short enough to track intraday regime shifts (e.g., pre-event vs post-event calm). This is the denominator for range_ratio — the analog of spread_sma in the original.

indicators.name: range_ratio
indicators.purpose: Ratio of current bar range to 5-min average range — direct analog of the original's spread_ratio = spread_bps / spread_sma. When ratio > 2.0, the current bar is 2x wider than recent average, signaling a microstructure stress event. The ratio normalizes for time-of-day volatility (morning vs afternoon). Same expansion threshold (2.0) as original because it represents the same empirical phenomenon.

indicators.name: peak_ratio_12
indicators.purpose: Rolling maximum of range_ratio over 12 bars (60 seconds). Detects whether there was a stress event (range_ratio > expansion_threshold) in the recent past 60 seconds. The original used spread_contracting = 'spread_ratio < spread_ratio[1] AND spread_ratio[1] > 2.0' — a point check. At 5s resolution we need to check the recent window because the peak may have passed 10-30 seconds ago. 12 bars (60s) matches our hold time: we only fade if the stress event was recent enough that the reversion hasn't already happened.

indicators.name: momentum_6
indicators.purpose: 30-second (6-bar) price return — the directional move that occurred during or immediately after the range expansion event. Analog of the original's post_event_return. At 5s resolution, 30 seconds captures the price displacement from the stress burst. If momentum_6 < -threshold, price dropped during the event (fade with CE). If > +threshold, price rose (fade with PE). 6 bars chosen because it spans the typical duration of a NIFTY stress event (15-30 seconds at the center of the range expansion period) while being long enough to measure a meaningful directional displacement.

conditions: peak_ratio_12 > expansion_threshold (2.0) — there was a range expansion event in the last 60s
range_ratio < contraction_threshold (1.5) — current bar range is back near normal
momentum_6 < -momentum_threshold (-0.0005) — price dropped ≥0.05% (~11 NIFTY pts) during/after event
buy_ce.confirmation: All three conditions true simultaneously; VIX < 22.0

conditions: peak_ratio_12 > expansion_threshold (2.0) — there was a range expansion event in the last 60s
range_ratio < contraction_threshold (1.5) — current bar range is back near normal
momentum_6 > +momentum_threshold (+0.0005) — price rose ≥0.05% (~11 NIFTY pts) during/after event
buy_pe.confirmation: All three conditions true simultaneously; VIX < 22.0

exit.stop_rationale: If the initial directional move that triggered entry extends by a further 10 NIFTY spot points after entry (≈5 option pts at ATM delta 0.5), the stress event is not an overshoot but a genuine informed directional move — the thesis is wrong and we exit immediately. NIFTY 1-minute typical move is 3-7 option pts; 5 pt stop is within that range, giving the trade minimal breathing room for noise while protecting against genuine trend continuation.
exit.target_rationale: A NIFTY stress event that displaced the index ~11+ spot pts is expected to revert 50-65% within 60 seconds as market-maker inventory rebalancing and VWAP-benchmark algo flow absorbs the overshoot. 50% reversion of 11 spot pts ≈ 5.5 option pts; we target 7 pts (≈14 spot pts reversion) to capture the upper end of the typical reversion, consistent with NIFTY 1-minute moves of 3-7 pts and giving 1:1.4 R:R.

filters.vix_filter: VIX < 22.0 — high VIX regimes produce structural range expansions from genuine macro stress; the reversion thesis requires that expansions are transient microstructure events, not regime-level volatility
filters.time_filter: 09:25-15:20 IST — skip first 10 minutes (structural spread widening at open) and last 10 minutes (EOD expiry dynamics)
filters.volume_filter: none — volume in 5s bars is too noisy on index; range expansion is the primary stress proxy
filters.trend_filter: none — fade both up and down spikes; the microstructure reversion thesis is symmetric
filters.spread_filter: range_ratio < contraction_threshold (1.5) at entry bar — must enter on contraction, not during expansion

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — range expansion/contraction is observable from OHLCV but the specific entry timing (contracting moment) requires 5s resolution that retail participants typically do not operate at. Edge could decay if HFT arbitrageurs systematically fade NIFTY spikes more aggressively.

adaptation_notes: The original strategy required real-time bid-ask spread data from individual NIFTY 50 constituent stocks (order_book: true, L1 data per stock) — unavailable in the pipeline. The core mechanism was ported by substituting the per-stock bid-ask spread with the NIFTY index's 5-second bar high-low range, which is a valid proxy for microstructure stress. The range_ratio = bar_range / avg_range_60 mirrors the original spread_ratio = spread_bps / spread_sma exactly. The post_event_return (original: price move since spread peak) is replaced by momentum_6 (30-second return), which captures the same directional displacement at 5s resolution. The original's 30-period spread SMA (30 min on 1-min bars) is compressed to 60-bar range average (5 min on 5s bars) because we're trading at 60s hold time, not 1-5 min. VIX filter retained at same threshold (22.0). The original's cross-sectional stock universe is replaced by NIFTY index alone — the same liquidity stress mechanism exists at the index level, driven by futures market makers rather than individual stock market makers.
weaknesses: Bar range expansion on NIFTY has many non-reversionary causes (data releases, RBI announcements, global macro prints) where the move IS the message — the fade thesis fails on informed events and no event calendar filter is implemented.
The range_ratio proxy is noisier than the true bid-ask spread — a wide 5-second bar could reflect a single large print mid-bar rather than systematic spread widening, reducing signal quality.
Signal frequency may be low (4-8 per day) if expansion events above 2x threshold are rare in calm sessions (VIX < 14), limiting the statistical power of backtests over 12 trading days.
